abstract: In this study, we propose to optimize the irradiated light in the front light structure for lensless fluorescence imaging devices by controlling the optical polarization. We fabricated strip diffraction on a thin-cover glass, which operates with a hybrid filter on the image sensor. The control of the excitation light polarization was coupled to diffractor substrates. The results confirm that the effect of $\mathbf{P}$ polarized light can significantly increase the intensity of irradiance light in front of the lensless imaging device, as observed through the contrast of the fluorescent beads.

articleTitle: Enhancing Complementary Split Ring Resonators Performance for Atherosclerosis Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper presents an improved complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) used as a non-invasive microwave sensor for in-vivo detection of atherosclerotic plaques. The sensor geometry was optimized on low-loss substrates to enhance the trade-off between the energy stored in the resonator and the energy radiated into the biological tissue. For positioning on the patient’s neck, the sensors were simulated in the presence of multilayer structures, and animal tissue samples were used for validation to estimate the penetration depth of the electromagnetic waves in these tissues. Finally, a three-dimensional model of the carotid artery was developed to extend the analysis beyond the tissues of the neck. The simulated results offer promising prospects for in-vivo diagnosis of carotid atherosclerotic plaques using these optimized CSRRs.

articleTitle: Bio-Inspired Sensor-Based Sound Pre-Processing for Speech Recognition in Noisy Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Despite tremendous research efforts in the field of speech recognition systems, current technologies cannot match the performance of human hearing in noisy environments. The recently introduced adaptive microelectromechanical (MEMS) cochlea [1] offers a potential solution here, as it performs signal (pre-)processing directly by the sensor, inspired by the functionality of the human cochlea. To show these advantages, we investigate here in a combined experimental and theoretical study, the speech recognition performance as a function of pre-processing. For speech recognition, a reservoir computing model based on memristive devices is used. For pre-processing, the MEMS cochlea is compared with a state-of-the-art Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) filter. For clean speech the system using MFCC filter has a slightly higher recognition efficiency than the one using the MEMS cochlea. In noisy environments, however, the MEMS cochlea is ahead. Thus, the MEMS cochlea-based pre-processing offers a route to hardware-implemented, edge computing for speech processing at the sensor node with high efficiency and low latency.

articleTitle: Fully Differential Dynamic Neural Amplifier: Preventing Saturation from Artifacts and Breaking the Gain-Bandwidth Trade-Off
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Neural recording is fundamental to advancements in neuroscience and the development of brain-computer interfaces. Central to this process is the neural amplifier, a critical component that directly influences the quality and fidelity of neural signal acquisition. The amplifier’s performance determines the noise level contaminating neural signals and ensures adequate amplification for accurate analog-to-digital conversion (ADC). However, conventional neural amplifiers face significant challenges. They typically require a constant biasing current, leading to inefficient power consumption, and are limited by a constrained gain-bandwidth product due to power budget restrictions. This paper addresses these challenges by delving into the essential requirements for neural amplifiers and discussing the limitations of traditional designs. We introduce a dynamic amplifier that not only surpasses the conventional gain-bandwidth trade-off but also effectively mitigates saturation issues caused by stimulation or motion artifacts. Furthermore, the proposed amplifier exhibits significantly lower thermal and $1 / \mathrm{f}$ noise compared to traditional static amplifiers. Our simulation results demonstrate that the proposed neural amplifier consumes less than 200 nW of power, with a signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) of 82.6 dB at a $\mathrm{5 k H z}$ bandwidth. The amplifier also achieves an input-referred noise of $4.54 \mu V_{\text {rms }}$. Additionally, the noise-efficient factor is 1.1, highlighting the amplifier’s noise performance and its suitability for high-fidelity neural signal acquisition.

articleTitle: Review of Non-invasive, Wearable Biomedical Sensor and Imaging IC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Technological innovation in biomedical science, driven by semiconductor circuit and system engineering, has enabled faster diagnosis, continuous health monitoring, and advanced treatment approaches. Recent advances in noninvasive, wearable biosensor interfaces and imaging have significantly improved performance and reduced costs, enhancing accessibility to medical technology. These sensors, benefiting from semiconductor technology, offer convenience, low infection risk, and cost-effective solutions for medical monitoring. This paper explores the principles, challenges, and advancements in non-invasive sensor technology, including electrodes, optical elements, and Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT). The integration of semiconductor technology in these applications is paving the way for personalized medicine and point-of-care solutions, with promising potential to improve patient care and healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: Brain network analysis reveals presentation rate dependent reorganizations during visual target detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: EEG-based target detection has attracted accumulating attention. However, understanding of the neural mechanisms from the perspective of functional connectivity alterations remains limited, especially under varying presentation rates - a crucial parameter in rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) tasks. Here, we conducted a RSVP experiment with two presentation rates (i.e., 200 and 400 ms) and employed graph theory to quantitatively investigate the brain network reorganization. The alterations of brain network were assessed at both global (i.e., $E_{g l o b}$ and $E_{l o c}$) and nodal (i.e., $E_{n o d a l}$) levels. As expected, mean accuracy at 200 ms rate was significantly lower than 400 ms. Distinct reorganizations between target and non-target stimuli at both global and nodal levels were observed between the two rates. Specifically, we observed significant increases in $E_{g l o b}$ and $E_{l o c}$ with higher presentation rates in the non-target stimuli. Moreover, channels with significant differences were mainly resided in the posterior parietal and occipital areas in $\gamma$ band. In sum, these results provide quantitative insights into the complex neural mechanisms involved in the target detection process.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: A Smart Ring for OSAHS Detection Based on Photoplethysmography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This demonstration presents a smart ring for obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) detection based on photoplethysmography (PPG), which integrates a PPG front-end circuit. Compared to the traditional polysomnography (PSG) method, the smart ring offers a more convenient, more portable and less invasive alternative. With the smart ring, users can directly view their overnight OSAHS events and apneahypopnea index (AHI) in the RingConn APP.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Modeling and Precision Analysis of Neural Recording System in Simulink
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: In recent years, multi-channel neural recording systems have become a popular research focus. The challenge in their design lies in balancing system performance, such as spike detection accuracy, with resource efficiency, including power consumption and area. To ensure accuracy while minimising design costs, it is crucial to investigate the specific impact of factors like nonlinearity on system accuracy. Therefore, we propose a nonlinear modeling method for neural recording systems using Simulink and a precision analysis method based on spike detection and sorting. Initially, we derive linear models for each system stage through transfer functions and introduce adjustable nonlinear gradients. Spike detection and sorting are then applied to the system output. We propose metrics to achieve this balance and analyze the relative impact of nonlinearities at each stage on the system. To achieve a $\pm 10 \%$ spike number error and $90 \%$ accuracy range, a total harmonic distortion as low as ${- 3 4. 3 2 d B},-33.73 \mathrm{~dB}$, and -44.42 dB is required for the low-noise amplifier (LNA), programmable gain amplifier (PGA), and analog-to-digital converter (ADC), respectively. This finding can guide efficient and performance-balanced hardware design for neural recording systems and is expected to be significantly less expensive to develop.

articleTitle: Flexible Electromagnetic-Lens for Wireless, Implantable Brain Machine Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Wireless power transfer has emerged as an essential requirement in implantable brain-machine interfaces (BMIs), providing significant advantages over traditional wired interfaces. However, challenges such as poor wireless power transfer efficiency, limited coverage area and transmission distance, safety, and interference with wireless communication hinder the widespread adoption of wireless power transfer in implantable BMIs. This paper demonstrates that two types of flexible electromagnetic lenses (EM-lens), which is an array of relay resonators formed as metamaterials, can significantly improve power transfer efficiency (PTE). The circular split ring resonator (C-SRR) based EM-lens outperforms in ex-vivo experiments with a $\mathbf{1 2. 0 7} \mathrm{dB}$ PTE enhancement from $\mathbf{0. 0 6 \%}$ to $\mathbf{1. 0 3 \%}$. The square resonator based EM-lens outperforms in air, improving the PTE from $\mathbf{0. 6 6 \%}$ to $\mathbf{1 6. 5 8 \%}$. Additionally, EM-lenses placed at two different locations in the subcutaneous and epidural regions are simulated in HFSS to determine the optimal placement. The simulations indicate that epidural placement could achieve higher PTE $\mathbf{4. 5 3 \%}$ but with increased specific absorption rate (SAR) as a trade-off. Finally, measurements of PTE versus location misalignment show that the EM-lens can maintain power coverage up to 88.58% of the lens area; and improve the power transmission distance by a factor of $\mathbf{5 3. 8 5 \%}$ compared to a single transmitter configuration.

articleTitle: A wide dynamic range, high-resolution multi-step SAR CDC for implanted humidity sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper proposes a wide dynamic range, high-resolution multi-step successive-approximation-register-based capacitance-to-digital converter (CDC) designed for characterizing implanted humidity sensors. The CDC features three conversion phases: a coarse phase with a LSB $=100 \mathrm{fF}$ for canceling large initial capacitance, a fine phase with a $L S B=1$ fF for detecting small variable capacitance, and an optional oversampling-with-integration phase for further enhancing the measurement resolution. The fine phase operates continuously while the coarse phase is only occasionally activated, i.e., during the initial quantization of an unknown capacitor or when the fine conversion exceeds its intended range. This operating strategy not only conserves power but also reduces conversion time. The simulation results show that the CDC has an effective resolution of 13.8 bits with 5 -time oversampling and 12.86 bits without oversampling.

articleTitle: A 4.4μW Cuffless Blood Pressure Measurement Processor Based on Event-Driven and Module-Level Asynchronous Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper proposes a cuffless blood pressure measurement processor based on photoplethysmogram (PPG) signals and deep neural networks (DNN). To reduce system power consumption, a module-level asynchronous scheme is designed. Moving average filter, feature extraction, and DNN computation units are all driven sequentially using event-driven wake-up. The moving average filtering unit is driven by a signal detector, which consists of a comparator and a counter. Each unit operates at different frequencies, effectively reducing the overall power consumption. The processor achieves mean error of $4.9 \pm 6.2$ mmHg and $3.4 \pm 4.4 \mathrm{mmHg}$ for systolic blood pressure (SBP) and diastolic blood pressure (DBP), respectively. Designed with a standard 55 nm CMOS technology, the digital core occupies an area of $0.64 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$, operates at a voltage of 1.2 V, with an estimated power consumption of $4.4 \mu \mathrm{~W}$.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Command-Driven SAR ADC for Implantable Cardiac Pacemakers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Most conventional ADCs sample the signal at a fixed sampling rate $\left(f_{s}\right)$, leading to either loss of the peak information of the cardiac signal (for low $f_{\mathrm{s}}$) or unnecessary redundant data and power consumption (for high $f_{\text {s }}$) when used to convert ECG signals. This paper presents a command-driven SAR ADC aiming to support those adaptive- $f_{\text {s }}$ algorithms for low-energy and high-quality acquisition of ECG signals. Upon receiving a quantization command pulse (QCP), the proposed asynchronous SAR ADC converts the signal tracked on its capacitive DAC (CDAC) into digits immediately without a specific sampling phase. Once the conversion completes, the ADC turns into the default tracking mode with zero power consumption and waits for the next QCP. A low-leakage rising-edge delay cell is also proposed to reduce power consumption of the SAR logic circuit further. Fabricated in a $180-\mathrm{nm}$ CMOS process with an active area of $0.087 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$, the ADC achieves 59.4-dB SNDR and 76.1-dB SFDR at 1-kSPS $f_{\mathrm{s}}$ while consuming 227 nW under 2 V supply voltage. When the ADC is used to sample the ECG signal with an adaptive $2-f_{\text {s }}$ strategy (100 SPS or 1 kSPS), the compression factor is 7.6, and the ADC power consumption is only 38 nW, achieving a power saving factor of 83%.

articleTitle: Surrogate Model Supported Optimization of high-definition Temporal Interference Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Temporal interference stimulation is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique using two or more electrodes to generate an electrical field, targeting deep brain structures. High-definition temporal interference stimulation enhances the focality and intensity of stimulation in specific regions. However, optimizing electrode positions remains challenging in TI stimulation. Typically, predefined discrete electrode positions are used, resulting in suboptimal outcomes due to the limited exploration of continuous positions. We address this by optimizing electrode placement freely on the head surface, leveraging high-fidelity simulations of the electrical field. To manage computational complexity, we propose using a neural network to approximate the mapping from continuous electrode positions to stimulation intensity in the target region. This surrogate model is used in the optimization process, significantly reducing computing time. Our results show that optimization based on the surrogate model for continuous electrode positions enhances stimulation performance, balancing intensity and focality.

articleTitle: DCLNet: Data Closed-Loop Network for Laryngoscopy Image Annotation and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Laryngeal diseases diagnosis is a common challenge in medical image processing. Traditional methods usually use classification networks to process entire images or their cropped key area images. However, the former may not effectively focus on the crucial region within the image, while the latter is a two-stage task that cannot utilize global information. To address this problem, we propose a novel Data Closed-Loop Network (DCLNet) for laryngoscope image classification, fully utilizing the global features in the image and enabling end-to-end training. By introducing attention mechanisms, DCLNet can automatically expand the Laryngoscope 8 classification dataset into a high-quality annotated object detection dataset. Moreover, to address some inherent issues of medical datasets, such as poor interpretability and a long-tailed distribution, we employ the methods of data closed-loop and curriculum learning. In this way, performance on the baseline dataset can be improved by optimizing the annotation of the training set without changing the model structure. Extensive experiments prove that our model achieves better performance compared to existing traditional methods.

articleTitle: The delay optimization for the alpha rhythm phase-locked neuromodulation system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Closed-loop neuromodulation systems have gained significant attention due to their ability to adapt stimulation parameters based on real-time brain activity, potentially reducing individual variability and enhancing treatment efficacy compared to open-loop approaches. This study investigates the impact of system latency on the performance of alpha rhythm phase-locked neuromodulation systems. Offline analysis revealed that signal transmission delays significantly affect phase estimation accuracy. A comparison between BrainAmp and OpenBCI EEG devices showed notable differences in latency, with BrainAmp exhibiting a latency of $74.4 \pm 7.9 \mathrm{~ms}$ while the embedded OpenBCI system achieved minimal transmission delays ($\lt \lt 1 \mathrm{~ms}$). Online implementation demonstrated that despite OpenBCI’s lower signal quality, its reduced transmission delays resulted in higher accuracy in phase estimation at the 0 -moment, with Mean Absolute Circular Error (MACE) values improving by over 0.25 in both eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. The findings emphasize the importance of minimizing system latencies in closed-loop neuromodulation systems to enhance the effectiveness of phaselocked stimulation. By addressing both algorithmic sophistication and system latency, this research contributes to the development of more precise and efficient neuromodulation techniques for applications in neurological and psychiatric disorders.

articleTitle: An IoT-Empowered Portable Monitoring System for EHG Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Preterm birth poses significant health risks, and its early detection is essential for preventing adverse outcomes. This study introduces a novel portable and remote monitoring system tailored for the analysis of electrohysterography (EHG) signals in a home-based setting. The system comprises four main components: a sensing device, an edge device, an Internet of Things (IoT) platform, and an EHG extraction algorithm. The sensing device is designed to capture, process, and transmit 4channel EHG signals effectively. The edge device includes a USB dongle to facilitate receiving wireless data. The IoT platform enables real-time data transmission either locally or remotely, providing healthcare professionals with key insights into uterine activity for better decision-making. The EHG signal extraction algorithm is used to extract EHG signals in four directions for analysis. In conclusion, the proposed system facilitates remote monitoring, allowing for clear observation of both the frequency and direction of uterine contractions.

articleTitle: An 8-Channel Fully Wirelessly Powered and Controlled Chip for Simultaneous ECG, EMG, and EOG Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper presents an eight-channel wirelessly powered and configured SoC for diverse biosignal sensing. An inductive 40.68 MHz link transfers power and clock signals to the chip, while data transmission from the chip is achieved using a UWB Tx in combination with an SMDL antenna, enabling communication over a distance of 4.3 m at 433 MHz. The chip consumes 170 uW (at $1 \mathrm{kSa} / \mathrm{s}$, eight channels) which can be scaled down to 70 uW (at $1 \mathrm{kSa} / \mathrm{s}$, single channel) by wirelessly disabling unused channels or lowering the sampling rate. To the author’s knowledge, this work is the first demonstration of simultaneous ECG, EMG, and EOG sensing in a fully wireless format.

articleTitle: An Unsupervised and Real-Time Spike Sorting Processor based on Digital Perturbed K-means Spike Sorting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Next-generation spike sorting processor needs to deal with extremely high data input. Hence a high-accuracy and low-area processor is critical for multi-channel implantable neural recording systems. In this study, we propose a spike sorting processor based on a novel architecture that runs unsupervised and in real-time. It features an adaptive-threshold spike detection that is based on a Sigma-Delta Control Loop and a novel spike classifier based on perturbed K-means. The test results show that the spike sorting processor has achieved an accuracy of over 93.2% on widely used synthetic datasets and real neural signal tests. The system has been synthesized using a 180-nm CMOS process, and our resource analysis reveals that it consumes just $2.56 \mu \mathrm{~W}$ per channel with a $1.8-\mathrm{V}$ supply, with a core area of $0.056 \mathrm{~mm}^{2} \mathrm{per}$ channel.

articleTitle: An Amplitude and Slope Based Nonlinearity Calibration Algorithm for LC-ADC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Level-crossing analog-to-digital converter (LC-ADC) has attracted widespread attention because of its eventdriven characteristic which boosts the energy efficiency by shrinking the amount of the data to be handled by the digital backend. However, the resolution of the LC-ADC is often less than 10 bits due to nonlinearities such as comparator offset and DAC mismatch. This paper proposes a calibration algorithm to compensate those various nonlinearities. It utilizes the signal amplitude and slope information to avoid too much storage of calibration parameters. The algorithm is verified by the post-layout simulation of a LC-ADC showing over 10dB signal-to-noise distortion ratio (SNDR) improvement. Finally, a LC-ADC with over 70 dB SNDR and 4 ksps equivalent Nyquist sampling rate is achieved drawing $8.3 \mu \mathrm{~A}$ current from 1.8V supply.

articleTitle: A Deep-Learning-Enabled Monitoring System for Recognizing G-induced Loss of Consciousness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Loss of consciousness induced by persistent positive acceleration is a significant hidden danger threatening the safety of maneuvering flight, necessitating timely and accurate monitoring and warnings. However, traditional monitoring systems for loss of consciousness primarily rely on electrophysiological signals, which are affected by vibration, electromagnetic interference, and other factors during actual flight. Consequently, these measurements are prone to external interference and lack robustness. To address these issues, we propose an automatic loss-of-consciousness monitoring system (ALOCMS) based on computational vision. This system utilizes the time-series features of the pilot’s head posture to identify the pilot’s state of consciousness effectively. To enhance the model’s generalization ability, we built a head pose dataset specific to flight scenarios and merged it with a public dataset for training the network model. Additionally, we developed a user-friendly human-computer interface to display monitoring information intuitively. Experimental results demonstrate that this system can accurately recognize and alert loss of consciousness in real time.

articleTitle: An Orthogonal Code-Division Multiplexing AFE with low Channel-Gain-Mismatch by Input Capacitors Calibration Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: An orthogonal code-division multiplexing analog front-end (AFE) for electroencephalogram (EEG) acquisition with low inter-channel gain mismatch is proposed in this paper. By adopting an orthogonal code-division multiplexing scheme based on Walsh-Hadamard codes, the area and power consumption of the circuit are effectively saved and the crosstalk between channels is maximally suppressed. In addition, an input capacitor calibration technique is proposed to improve the match of the capacitors by calibrating the input capacitors of each channel successively. The proposed AFE was fabricated in a 65 nm CMOS process. The measured results show that the gain range is $34-60 \mathrm{~dB}$, and the gain mismatch of the multi-channel AFE is reduced to 0.33%.

articleTitle: A Power-Efficient LDO with Slew-Rate-Enhanced Amplifier and Buffer for Biomedical Applications with High-Frequency Load Transient
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: In this paper, a low-power, fast-transient and low dropout regulator (LDO) is proposed for high-frequency load transient in biomimetic electrical stimulation medical devices. The implementation of a dynamic recycling folded cascode (DRFC) amplifier alone with a dynamic rail-to-rail adaptive buffer (DRAB) reduces power transistor’s dimension and enhances the transient performance. The LDO is implemented with 55 nm CMOS process. With an output capacitor of $2.2 \mu \mathrm{~F}$ and under the load step between 0 and 150 mA, post-simulation results show that the undershoot and overshoot of high-frequency load transient ($10 \mu \mathrm{~s}$ heavy/light load duration) is 43 mV and 35 mV, respectively. The proposed regulator consumes $5.1 \mu \mathrm{~A}$ quiescent current, achieving 99.97% equivalent current efficiency at 150 mA load current.

articleTitle: Accuracy of RingConn Smart Ring in Sleep Assessment Compared to Polysomnography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Wearable devices have attracted significant interest from consumers and researchers due to their ability to cost-effectively estimate sleep patterns in everyday living conditions. Smart rings have gained significant attention among these devices for their portability and comfortable wearing experience. The RingConn Smart Ring, launched by Shenzhen Ninenovo Technology Limited, has attracted many users with its unique design and user experience. However, the efficacy of sleep data assessment by RingConn has not been directly compared to the gold standard polysomnography (PSG). In this study, the accuracy of the RingConn was evaluated in comparison to the PSG. A dataset jointly collected by RingConn LLC and Shanghai Ruijin Hospital was used. Subjects wore both PSG and RingConn, and the results were compared to assess the accuracy of RingConn in monitoring the user’s sleep. The results show that RingConn demonstrated good performance with comparable accuracy in sleep assessment. The MAE of sleep Heart Rate is 2.27 BPM, the MAE of Blood Oxygen Saturation is $\mathbf{0. 3 8 \%}$, and the MAE of Total Sleep Time is $\mathbf{1 2. 2 5} \mathbf{~ m i n}$. This suggests that RingConn has the potential to be widely used in home sleep monitoring.

articleTitle: A Fast Square Wave-based Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy for Impedance-based Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper introduces a fast, high-accuracy methodology for conducting Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) based on Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), in order to meet the requirements of portable, real-time biomedical impedance-based detections. Instead of using white noise-like wideband signals as in conventional FFT-based EIS, the proposed method uses a square wave as the sensor excitation signal. This approach achieves a fast EIS measurement, but no longer requires complex circuits like high-resolution DACs or frequency mixers for the signal generation. The conditions where the sensor behaves like a pseudo electronic Linear Time-Invariance (LTI) circuit are firstly identified by investigating its large-signal behavior, Cyclic Voltammetry (CV), which ensures the sensor shows no potential-amplitude dependence, hence also providing possibilities for other novel EIS circuitry. A circuit consisting of a control amplifier and a Trans-Impedance Amplifier (TIA) is designed and fabricated with 65 nm CMOS to implement this methodology for validating its on-chip feasibility. This work shortens the EIS measurement time by 91.7% in a frequency sweep range from 0.5 Hz to 500 Hz, with only 1.48% average Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), compared to a commercial chemical instrument AutoLab, which ensures this method is suitable for portable, real-time EIS biomedical detections and applications.

articleTitle: Multi-scale Lung CT Image Registration Based on Mamba-ConvNet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: To address the issue of large deformations in medical image registration, we proposed a novel multi-scale lung CT image registration method based on Mamba-ConvNet. By effectively learning multi-scale features and incorporating long-range modeling, the capability of the registration network in dealing with complex deformations is improved. Furthermore, to preserve the topology of transformation, we adopt diffeomorphic deformation with a stationary velocity field, resulting in a more accurate deformation vector field (DVF). Experiment results on the DIR-Lab dataset demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over current deep learning-based methods in terms of target registration error (TRE), especially in cases with large initial deformations, the proposed method improves by 37%.

articleTitle: A Novel ECG-based Dynamic Encryption Scheme for WBANs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Data security has become a critical issue limiting the rapid development of Wireless Body Area Networks (WBANs). Conventional encryption methods are considered not feasible for WBAN scenarios due to the complexity of the algorithms. Physiological signal-based encryption methods are believed to be potential solutions for WBANs due to the natural randomness of the data. However, physiological data has the drawbacks of high correlation and small key space within a short period. In this paper, a novel Electrocardiogram (ECG)based dynamic encryption scheme for WBANs is proposed. By utilizing the similarity of ECG features in various locations, a novel key distribution method based on security templates is proposed to synchronize the key seeds securely. Then, the designed multidimensional chaotic system dynamically generates key sequences by synchronizing key seeds among different nodes to en/decrypt the information in WBANs. The validation and analysis results demonstrate that the scheme has the advantages of large key space, high randomness and robustness, and low latency compared to the existing methods.

articleTitle: MEGA: A Multimodal EEG-Based Visual Fatigue Assessment System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: SSVEP-BCI are renowned for their high precision, rapid data transmission, and the advantage of not requiring user training. However, the intense brightness, frequent lowfrequency stimuli, and monotony of tasks required for SSVEP signal generation can lead to visual fatigue. This paper addresses the issue of visual fatigue within SSVEP-based BCI systems. We introduce a real-time fatigue assessment system named MEGA, which features a high-precision, wearable EEG device engineered with ARM architecture. The system employs a multimodal fusion classification algorithm, enhancing the comfort and performance of the SSVEP-BCI system during operation. By analyzing characteristics from EEG channels O1, O2, Fp1, and Fp2, extracting blink features using STFT, and integrating EEG entropy, we have explored a robust set of fatigue classification features. This streamlined and sensitive feature combination reduces system complexity while improving classifier sensitivity. The proposed multimodal transformer architecture for fatigue classification aims to enhance both the comfort and performance during SSVEP-BCI system operation. Ultimately, the proposed system achieved a classification accuracy of $\mathbf{9 8. 8 9 \%}$, which is 4.89% higher than the latest visual fatigue classification systems.

articleTitle: Efficient Epileptic Seizure Type Classification Using Hyperdimensional Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Precise seizure identification plays a vital role in understanding cortical connectivity and informing treatment decisions. Yet, the manual diagnostic methods for epileptic seizures are both labor-intensive and highly specialized. In this study, we propose a Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) classifier for accurate and efficient multi-type seizure classification. Despite previous seizure analysis efforts using HDC being limited to binary detection (seizure or no seizure), our work breaks new ground by utilizing HDC to classify seizures into multiple distinct types. HDC offers significant advantages, such as lower memory requirements, a reduced hardware footprint for wearable devices, and decreased computational complexity. Due to these attributes, HDC can be an alternative to traditional machine learning methods, making it a practical and efficient solution, particularly in resource-limited scenarios or applications involving wearable devices. We evaluated the proposed technique on the latest version of TUH EEG Seizure Corpus (TUSZ) dataset and the evaluation result demonstrate noteworthy performance, achieving a weighted $F 1$ score of $\mathbf{9 4. 6 \%}$. This outcome is in line with, or even exceeds, the performance achieved by the state-of-the-art traditional machine learning methods.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient Adaptive-Frequency-Modulated PPG Acquisition Circuits with Power-on-Demand Trans-impedance Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Photoplethysmoggraphy (PPG) is a non-invasive technique used to detect blood volume changes in the microvascular bed of issues. It is commonly used in wearable devices and medical monitoring systems to measure heart several vital signs, such as blood oxygen saturation, blood preasure and heart rate. Frequency modulation (FM) is one of the efficiency approaches to mitigate the SNR degeneration due to motion artifacts. However, FM results in higher required bandwidth in the acquisition circuits which leads to a higher overhead in power consumption, especially when remaining stationary for extended periods. In this paper, an adaptive-frequency-modulated scheme together with a power-on-demand trans-impedance amplifier (TIA) is proposed. Which enables a power-on-demand strategy to maintain sufficient SNR with minimum modulation frequency as well as the circuit bandwidth. The experimental results shows a 37% power saving in typical scenarios compared to conventional fixed-frequency PPG acquisition circuits.

articleTitle: Enhancing Respiratory Sound Detection Through Integrated Learning and Dynamic Convolutional Recurrent Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This study introduces an integrated learning approach for the classification of breath sounds and event detection, leveraging Mel-scale frequency cepstrum coefficients (MFCC) to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of sound event detection. The method employs MFCC to characterize the filtered sound signal, alongside dynamic frequency convolution and Dynamic Triple Center Loss (DTCL) for feature extraction and classification. Experiments conducted on the SPRSound database demonstrate the efficacy of MFCC feature extraction in enhancing model performance. Specifically, the Dynamic Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (DCRNN) achieves the highest F score and the lowest Equivalent Error Rate (ER) when utilizing the triple center loss method. These findings underscore the substantial improvement in breath sound detection facilitated by the proposed method, thereby paving the way for advancements in audio signal processing and sound event detection.

articleTitle: An Area-Energy Efficient EEG Detection System Based On PWL and Nonlinear SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a low-power and area-efficient detection chip design for Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification of EEG signals. The design incorporates a 256-point FFT module for feature extraction of EEG signals. To further reduce power consumption and circuit complexity, an approximate computing approach is introduced for operations such as energy calculation, exponential functions and squaring. Additionally, a custom compression-based Lagrange multiplier encoding technique is employed. The proposed detection system has been implemented on FPGAs, achieving a $\mathbf{1 0 \% - 3 0 \%}$ reduction in resource utilization compared to recent related works, with power consumption as low as 0.201 W, significantly lower than existing solutions. In chip design, the energy efficiency reaches $0.31 \mu \mathrm{~J} /$ Class, which is an improvement of over 25%, and the area is reduced by more than 40%. Overall, the proposed detection system effectively reduces resource and power consumption through approximate computing circuits and encoding methods.

articleTitle: fNIRS-based Monitoring of Functional Brain Network during Image Guided Hand Movements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This study investigated the effects of image guidance on uni- and bi-manual movements using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), a pivotal wearable system for optical neuroimaging. We analyzed fNIRS signals from seven participants performing three motor tasks: left finger tapping, right finger tapping, and finger crossing under three conditions: motor execution, motor imagery, and guided motor imagery (GMI). Moreover, the motor and prefrontal cortices’ functional connectivity, and brain networks were compared. Obtained results demonstrated that bimanual movements elicit tighter functional connections than unimanual movements. Additionally, image guidance made motor imagery more similar to actual movements under various features. Furthermore, the achieved results are the highest classification accuracy of 0.896 from GMI among the three motor conditions using a hybrid strategy of 5-channel statistical and 9-channel functional brain network features. Also, the outcome of this study provides insights into the functional connectivity and brain networks involved in various motor tasks, with implications for rehabilitation training and brain-machine interface applications.

articleTitle: A High Dynamic Range Hybrid CT/DT Delta-Sigma Modulator for Medical X-ray Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper proposes a high dynamic range $4^{\text {th }}$-order $\Delta-\Sigma$ modulator (DSM) designed for column-parallel readout analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) in medical X-ray detectors. The design achieves improved power and area efficiency and better robustness against clock jitter and process mismatch by using a hybrid continuous-time (CT) and discrete-time (DT) loop filter structure. The adoption of non-delayed DT integrators stabilizes the system and expands the maximum stable amplitude (MSA) to up to 0.7 Vpp under a 1.8 V power supply. The bandwidth of the proposed DSM is 24 kHz. With the presence of process mismatch, the implemented DSM can still achieve a dynamic range (DR) of about 96 dB with a 6.144 MHz sampling rate. The power consumption of the DSM is estimated as around $486.5 ~ \mu W$ by using a standard $180-\mathrm{nm}$ CMOS process.

articleTitle: A 1.01μVrms, 16.5bit ECG Acquisition IC with Embedded DC-Servo-Loop and Multi Channel Discharge Dynamic Comparator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-precision ECG acquisition analog front-end (AFE) with a capacitively-coupled chopper instrumentation amplifier (CCIA), a LPF and a noise-shaping delta sigma ADC. The CCIA employs an embedded DC-servo loop to reduce input-referred noise (IRN) and incorporates self-regulating bias and common-mode replication techniques to enhance the common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR). The input stage of the delta sigma ADC utilizes the substrate-biasing bootstrap switch to mitigate body effects, thereby improving linearity and signal-to-noise ratio. The output stage utilizes a multi channel discharge dynamic comparator with a preamplifier stage that suppresses kickback noise. The CCIA achieved 1.01 $\mu V_{r m s}$ IRN from 0.5 to 150 Hz and 96.54 dB CMRR. The ADC achieved 16.5 effective number of bit (ENOB) within a 1 k bandwidth. The AFE is implemented in a $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ CMOS process and consumes $33.4 \mu W$ from a 1.8 V supply.

articleTitle: Low-Complexity and Efficient Spike Sorting Algorithm Implemented on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Next-generation neural interface systems will have an increasing number of channels and higher resolution to process signals from thousands of neurons. Online spike sorting is an effective method to ease the data bandwidth bottleneck. However, existing algorithms with high accuracy often have higher computational complexity in feature extraction. This paper presents a novel feature extraction method for spike sorting. The method is implemented on a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) to verify its performance. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm achieves high classification accuracy while compressing signals, without leading to a significant increase in computation or resource utilization.

articleTitle: Wearable High-Density sEMG Processing with Class Activation Maps with an Embedded Temporal Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: High-density surface electromyography (HD-sEMG) holds promise for advancing intuitive and non-invasive human-machine interfaces (HMIs) due to its higher spatial resolution compared to sparse sEMG. We address the challenge of integrating the HD-sEMG’s data volume with embedded computing to enable fully wearable control systems. We target HD-sEMG data from the wearable EMaGer $\mathbf{4} \times 16$ sensors system, with a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) that processes all channels and yields $(94.7 \pm 1.2) \%$ accuracy on 6 classes. Moreover, we analyze the TCN’s $4 \times 16$ Class Activation Maps with an approach inspired by computer vision, showing that channel relevance has a rowwise behavior not shown before. We deploy our TCN on the parallel ultra-low-power GAP9 MCU, consuming only 28.7 mW, 13.7 uJ per inference, and 475 us inference computation time, compatible with the constraints of real-time processing. Our work advances the SoA in the integration of HD-sEMG and embedded computing for wearable HMIs by combining wearable HD acquisition and embedded inference.

articleTitle: Compression of Respiratory Sound Signals via TranscoderQVAE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Respiratory diseases are one of the most common causes of death worldwide. At present, digital stethoscopes are valuable tools for diagnosing respiratory diseases, but they face limitations in storage, computation, and transmission capabilities. Therefore, developing respiratory sound compression algorithms is crucial. In this work, we propose TranscoderQVAE (TQVAE). TQVAE adopts the idea of variational autoencoder, non-uniform quantizer and Transformer to perform compression and recovery tasks on respiratory sounds Based on the concept of compressive sensing, we use an encoder to reduce data points and a nonuniform quantizer to compress the signal to 4 bits and stored which can reduce the storage space. Finally, we use a simplified Transformer as a decoder named Transcoder to recover signals. Meanwhile, a denoising algorithm based on wavelet transformation is applied to the recovered signal to remove noise. Through performing experiments of 3554 pieces of data, the correlation coefficient between the recovered signal and the raw signal can reach $\mathbf{0. 9 8}$. And the compression ratio can reach up to 256. Other evaluation metrics are also terrific. The algorithm execution time is less than 13 seconds per signal.

articleTitle: Topological Nonlinear Analysis of Dynamical Systems for Patient-Ventilator Asynchrony Events Recognition in Mechanical Ventilation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Mechanical ventilation is critical to patients suffering from respiratory disorders. However, patient-ventilator asynchrony(PVA) events seriously impact patients’ comfort in rehabilitation or treatment progress and, sometimes, threaten clinical safety. Thus, detecting and altering abnormal mechanical ventilation events are vital in biomedical state monitoring. This paper proposes a topological nonlinear analysis approach to identifying PVA events, addressing the recognition challenge during mechanical ventilation. The proposed approach distinguished itself in the experimental validations performed with clinical data collected from 22 subjects for recognizing common PVA events, including double triggering, ineffective efforts, premature cycling, and delayed cycling. The proposed topological feature shows advantages compared to other related nonlinear dynamics descriptors, which is supposed to be a novel solution for PVA analysis.

articleTitle: A High-Precision Implantable Neuromodulation Device for Closed-Loop Deep Brain Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Closed-loop deep brain stimulation, a critical technology in brain-machine interfaces, offers a promising treatment for neurological disorders. This paper presents a high-precision closed-loop deep brain stimulation device that allows simultaneous stimulation and recording on the same or adjacent electrode sites. To achieve high-precision closed-loop control, this work utilizes a custom neuromodulation integrated circuit incorporating Redundant-Crossfire stimulator and Frequency Shaping & Quick Blanking based front-end interface. Measurement results show that the stimulation precision reaches 9.3 bits with an 8 channel configuration (13.1 bits for a 4 -channel configuration). When recording LFPs in the range of $1-100 \mathrm{~Hz}$, the total input reference noise of the system is $3.98 \mu \mathrm{~V}$. In addition, long-term animal experiments conducted in pigs demonstrate that the system effectively suppresses external interference and artifacts, providing an effective solution for extended DBS applications.

articleTitle: Compressed Plane-Wave Compounding for Efficient Imaging on Portable Ultrasound Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Sub-Nyquist sampling, also known as compressive sensing (CS), leverages the sparsity of ultrasound signals to reduce the sampling rate required for accurate ultrasound image reconstruction. Such under-sampling can reduce the computational complexity of the reconstruction algorithm while also relaxing on-board memory requirements. This paper demonstrates up to $10 \times$ reduction in total sample count by applying CS algorithms to ultrasound imaging using coherent plane-wave compounding (CPWC), and up to $57 \times$ reduction for single plane waves by combining CS with convolution beamforming. The resulting compression facilitates processing of the acquired samples directly on portable ultrasound devices, thus eliminating the need to transmit the data to a remote cloud for processing. The proposed compressed CPWC imaging approach is suitable for efficient target localization during focused ultrasound (FUS) neuromodulation. A portable ultrasound system for FUS neuromodulation, based on a system-on-chip (SoC) module and equipped with a dual-mode wearable probe, is also presented.

articleTitle: A CMOS Wireless Synchronization and Control System for Sensor Modules in MRI Scanners
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Monitoring motion in a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) environment safely and reliably requires placing wireless nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) sensors in the bore. This paper proposes an integrated circuit capable of achieving phase synchronization and creating triggering events for such sensors. It relies on the transmission of a Radio Frequency (RF) tone with amplitude modulation (AM). A variable-gain amplifier (VGA) compensates for the path loss of the broadcasted RF signal in the scanner room. A divider-less bang-bang phase-locked loop (BBPLL) based on a digitally controlled crystal oscillator (DCXO) achieves phase lock with a sub-picosecond integrated jitter. Lastly, an envelope detector processes the two-level amplitude-shift keying (ASK) AM on the RF signal to control subsequent sensors. The overall system is integrated into a 65 nm CMOS process and exhibits a power consumption of 5.2 mW in an area smaller than $1.5 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ with a sensitivity of -57 dBm.

articleTitle: A 45μW Ultrasonic Implantable Wireless Neural Recording Chip Featuring Simultaneous Power Transmission and Backscatter Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper presents an energy-efficient ultrasonic (US) implantable wireless neural-recording chip comprising a frequency-translating reconfigurable US backscatter modulator, a US power management unit, a clock generation unit, and a data acquisition unit. This is the first integrated circuit designed to enable high-throughput continuous US passive backscatter uplink communication at ultra-low power with uninterrupted US powering. The chip is fabricated in 65 nm CMOS with a total active area of $0.35 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. The proposed reconfigurable backscatter modulation achieved a maximum data rate of 220 kbps at ultralow power, resulting in efficiencies of $12.3 \mathrm{pJ} / \mathrm{bit}$ and $23.2 \mathrm{pJ} / \mathrm{bit}$ for OOK and BPSK, respectively, with US transducers spaced by 6 cm in water. This is the most efficient US communication, to our knowledge. The chip was validated in-vitro, with all blocks operating, the chip consumes only $45 \mu \mathrm{~W}$.

articleTitle: A Cross-Modal Contrastive Representation Learning Model for OSAHS Detection Based on Decoupling and Reconstruction Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome (OSAHS) significantly impacts public health and safety. Multimodal biomedical signals (MBS) are essential for OSAHS screening. However, current deep learning frameworks for MBS struggle to differentiate between modality-specific and shared information, leading to confusion and reduced model performance. Additionally, the heterogeneity of modalities and limited labeled data further hinder effective MBS modeling. To address these challenges, we propose a cross-modal contrastive learning method based on decoupling and reconstructing multimodal biomedical signals (CMDR). Specific encoders extract unique information from different modalities, while specific decoders handle modality reconstruction. A shared encoder then extracts patterns across modalities, using a cross-attention mechanism to decouple relationships and ensure orthogonality between modality-specific and shared features. Cross-modal contrastive learning is applied to the representations from each specific encoder, ensuring effective extraction and learning of modality-specific information. Finally, specific and shared features are fused, with a self-attention mechanism capturing both specificity and consistency of the signals. We validate CMDR on three multimodal biomedical signal datasets for OSAHS screening. Experimental results demonstrate that CMDR outperforms current baseline models, achieving an average F1-score improvement of 9.27%, setting a new state-of-the-art in OSAHS task performance.

articleTitle: A Fully Integreated Current-Mode LDO Using PSRC and APSR Technique With -71.8 dB PSRR at 6.78 MHz for Implantable Medical Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a fully integrated capacitor-less high PSRR LDO based on current-mode topology. A power supply ripple cancellation technique (PSRC) is proposed to improve the PSRR at high frequency. The PSRC is based on the flipped voltage follower (FVF) and the super source follower structure (SSF) is added to improve the stability of proposed LDO. The small signal of the PSRC technique is set up and the PSRR at low frequency is not affected in proposed LDO. In addition, an adjustable PSRR technique is achieved. The PSRR at the range from 100 kHz to 10 MHz can be greatly improved at a specific frequency by adjusting the value of the compensation resistance according to the working frequency of specific applications. The proposed LDO is designed in a $0.18 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ CMOS process, which achieves the PSRR of -79 dB at DC and -71.8 dB at 6.78 MHz. Moreover, the PSRR is enhanced by 30 dB at 126 MHz.

articleTitle: A Cryptographic Security Engine With Sequence Tracker for Implantable Neural Stimulation Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Neural stimulation devices have shown a significant impact on the treatment of neurological disorders such as Parkinson’s disease, epilepsy, and chronic pain. Maintaining secure communication with these devices is essential to keep the confidentiality and integrity of the patient’s data and the authenticity of the transmitter. The proposed work provides a framework for a power-aware security engine for such implantable devices by incorporating a cryptographic security engine to ensure the message’s confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity. While prior works focus on confidentiality, the proposed engine involves the use of AES-128 decryption and a sequence tracker to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity by disabling malicious repeat attacks to realize secure implantable neural stimulators. The security engine is tested and functionally verified on an FPGA and implemented in a CMOS 65 nm process, resulting in a $0.09 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ area and $45 \mu \mathrm{~W}$ power consumption.

articleTitle: Amplitude and Phase Errors Optimization for High-Precision Electrical Impedance Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Due to its non-invasive, deep sensing and radiationfree characteristics, electrical impedance measurement has become a key technique in empowering biological imaging and flexible sensing applications. However, large amplitude error and phase errors exist in conventional electrical impedance measurement system due to the harmonic error of demodulation and the limited bandwidth of the circuit, which will significantly affect the accuracy of the flexible sensing systems. A system level low amplitude and phase error optimization scheme is proposed with amplitude correction and pre-I/Q-demodulation. Behavior model is built to verify the error reduction of the proposed scheme. For the electrical impedance tomography application, behavior model simulation shows that the impedance is measured with 0.45% amplitude error and 0° phase error. Compared to the conventional system, the proposed scheme achieves a $\mathbf{7 4 \%}$ reduction of amplitude error and a 100% reduction of phase error.

articleTitle: A Wireless Injectable Device for Multimodal Animal Physiological Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a wireless multimodal physiological monitoring application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) fabricated in the 180 nm process and assembled in an injectable device to measure photoplethysmography (PPG), electrocardiography (ECG), and subcutaneous body temperature of animals. The device miniaturization is achieved by a shared receiver (Rx) coil and inductive link for both wireless power transfer (WPT) and data communication. An optimized folded Lshape Rx coil enhances the quality $(Q)$ factor, coupling with the transmitter (Tx) coil without increasing the device size. To facilitate WPT, the ASIC alternates between recording and lowpower sleep modes, achieving $2.54 \mu \mathrm{~W}$ ultra-low power consumption on average. The ECG analog frontend (AFE) amplifies the ECG signal with an adjustable gain of 45-80 dB and an input-referred noise (IRN) of $0.99 \mu \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{Rms}}$, while the PPG AFE achieves an IRN of 30.8 pArms. The temperature AFE provides a $27-47^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ sensing range with $0.02{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ inaccuracy. The AFE outputs are sequentially quantized by a 10-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) with 54.7 dB signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR). For reliable data transmission, the ASIC employs a memoryassisted backscatter scheme, storing data in an 8 Mb memory chip and transmitting it when the inductive link is stable. The ASIC functionality has been validated in vivo on anesthetized rats.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: Low-energy Unstructured Sparsity-aware Spiking Attention and Convolution SNN Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Demonstration Type — Prepublication. This is the companion demonstration of our paper titled “A $0.078 \mathrm{~pJ} / \mathrm{SOP}$ Unstructured Sparsity-Aware Spiking Attention/Convolution Processor with 3D Compute Array,” that was presented at the 2024 IEEE Custom Integrated Circuits Conference (CICC), Denver, CO, USA.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: Real-Time Gait and Respiration Analysis using Ultra-Wideband Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time algorithm developed for an ultra-wideband (UWB) radar sensor that performs comprehensive gait and respiration analysis. The method (1) estimates feet trajectory and respiration signals from radar data, (2) analyzes peak distributions and locations in the frequency spectrum, (3) identifies if either signal exhibits a sinusoidal waveform, (4) distinguishes between walking and pure breathing states based on signal characteristics, and (5) extracts clinically relevant features. The algorithm extracts spatiotemporal gait parameters for walking individuals, including step count, step length, cadence, and walking speed [1]. For stationary individuals, the system extracts the respiration rate along with a confidence level indicating whether the radar signal contains respiratory information or body-movement artifacts [2]. This demonstration highlights the potential of UWB radar technology as a dual-functional tool for continuous health monitoring applications, both in clinical and home environments. (Demo type: Academia)

articleTitle: A 64-channel Fully Implantable Brain-computer Microsystem with Custom Microelectrode Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a 64-channel fully implantable neural signal recording and processing system. The system is designed with hermetically sealed, commercial off-the-shelf components to enable neural signal acquisition, wireless transmitting and wireless charging. Additionally, an artificial neural network was implemented on the hardware to create a standalone, comprehensive brain signal decoding system. A silicon-based microelectrode array, fabricated with MEMS process and assembled into 3D floating form by stacking planar silicon probes, was attached to the system to sense neural signals. The whole system was militarized packaged into a medical-scale titanium case and embedded onto skull for brain-computer interface (BCI) applications. The study demonstrates the feasibility and potential of this advanced technology for neural signal recording and processing in a fully implantable system.

articleTitle: Desigh of Implantable Planar Monopole Antenna for 400 MHz 16-QAM Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This paper proposed a new compact implantable partially curved monopole antenna with a bandwidth covering 400-450 MHz. The transmitter’s titanium metal case is used as the reference ground. The antenna features a gain of −26.2 dBi, a bandwidth of $360-480 \mathrm{MHz}$, and a small volume of 11.4 $\mathbf{m m}^{3}$. Part of the proposed monopole antenna is shaped into a folded curved-line structure to increase the electrical length of the antenna without increasing its size. The proposed antenna is used for a 400 MHz 16-QAM transmitter designed for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: A Body Channel Communication Control Processor Utilizing Manchester Code
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Compared with conventional communication technologies, body channel communication (BCC) shows more security and better energy efficiency by utilizing the human body as a transmission medium. This paper presents an integrated BCC control processor including a transmitter, a receiver, and a data processing unit. Manchester coding is used with the advantages of less low-frequency interference and better use of the characteristics of the human body channel. Instead of using a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), data processing is integrated digitally to reduce the overall area and power consumption. The BCC control processor parameters can be configured flexibly via Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI), which is used more conveniently with other commercial chips. The proposed control processor has successfully implemented data transmission and processing with Manchester code and SPI protocol.

articleTitle: Dynamic pH fluctuations in cancer cells on CMOS-based Lab-on-Chip ISFET arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Early diagnosis of cancer is a key avenue to improving cancer incidence rates and prognosis. This paper presents a rapid assay for live, mammalian cancer cell culture on a Lab-on-Chip ISFET array fabricated in CMOS technology. Detection of osteosarcoma cells is recorded as a significant difference in endpoint $\mathbf{p H}$ on ISFET sensors. Control measurements of $\mathbf{p H}$ change in cell culture media due to any CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> supply fluctuations in an incubator allow compensation of non-ideal effects including sensor drift and baseline $\mathbf{p H}$ change associated with a bicarbonate buffering system. Distinguishing metrics, including total drift rate and standard deviation of sensor output are extracted and attributed to cell presence on-chip. Mean total drift rate shows an 89.7% difference between sample and control wells, aiding characterisation of cancer cell presence. Standard deviation captures the noise output attributed to cell culture on the sensor surface, reporting an $\mathbf{8 1. 4 \%}$ difference between populations. This Point-of-Care diagnostic device and assay for rapid cell detection on a Lab-on-Chip shows significant potential to provide a rapid and cost-effective diagnostic tool for live cell measurements.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: A Lab-on-Chip Platform for Dynamic Biosensing of Fluids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: We present a comprehensive Lab-on-Chip platform that integrates a CMOS ISFET array with a 3D-printed microfluidic flow cell. The sensing front end is a System-on-Chip, fabricated using an unmodified CMOS technology, which monolithically integrates the sensing array and its instrumentation circuits. A dedicated FPGA-based digital readout system manages data acquisition, buffering, and transmission. The platform supports temperature regulation through a feedback control loop and uses a peristaltic pump for monitoring samples across the ISFET sensing array during dynamic flow, allowing real-time investigation of ion reactions on the surface.

articleTitle: Wireless and Stretchable Multichannel Neural Interface Device Based on Conformal Parylene Thin-Film
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: In the field of brain-computer interfaces, implantable neural interface devices play a crucial role as powerful tools for acquiring high-quality electrophysiological signals which significantly influence the accuracy of the subsequent processing and feedback control. The paper presents a wireless and stretchable electrocorticography (ECoG) neural device based on biocompatible Parylene C polymer by incorporating serpentine metal interconnects. In vitro electrochemical measurements verified the excellent functionality of the neural electrodes, with impedances as low as $13 \pm 0.4 \mathrm{k} \Omega$ at 1 kHz, facilitating high-resolution neural recording. The mechanical and electrochemical properties have been investigated through repetitive stretching tests. The developed microelectrode array was capable of reliably and wirelessly recording the local field potentials in the primary motor cortex of the brain with an averaged amplitude of 50 $\mu \mathrm{V}$. An optimized active-matrix architecture has been proposed by incorporating high-performance silicon nanomembrane thin-film transistors (TFTs) into parylenebased electrode array. The corresponding sensing and switching characteristics were simulated using Cadence software to demonstrate the enormous potential for highfidelity detection of weak neural signals.

articleTitle: Wireless Intracranial Pressure Monitoring System based on Multi-layer Printed Coil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This work proposes a wireless intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring system based on a multi-layer printed coil (MLPC) inductive link. The system is composed of an implantable ICP sensor, a portable controller and a data management terminal. The ICP sensor in our previous work were powered by off-board coil, making the power supply the primary obstacle to implant miniaturization. This paper introduces an MLPC structure, and the corresponding model along with an inductive link based on it. The results show that an MLPC of the same size can provide $3 x$ quality factor of a printed spiral coil. PCB-integrated coil design reduces the size of the ICP sensor by 75% compared with previous work. The proposed ICP monitoring system achieves a 17 mm operating distance and a measurement resolution of $0.3 \mathbf{~ m m H g}$. Keywords-Intracranial pressure monitoring, multi-layer printed coil, wireless power transfer, implantable device

articleTitle: The LFP Responses in Primary Visual Cortex to Light Flickering Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Light flicker stimulation, particularly at 40 Hz, has gained significant attention for its potential as a rapid and non-invasive treatment for various neurological and psychiatric disorders. However, the factors of flicker stimulation that affect the neural responses in the primary visual cortex (V1) are not fully understood yet. In this study, we recorded local field potential (LFP) in the V1 of rats using microwire electrodes while presenting visual flicker stimulation. We studied the influence of the frequency, duty-cycle and wavelength of flicker stimulation. We found that the low-frequency flicker stimulation ($10 \mathrm{~Hz}, 20$ Hz), instead of 40 Hz, resulted in a more significant increase in LFP power at both the stimulation and harmonic frequencies rapidly. The most significant power increase was observed when applying $20 \mathrm{~Hz} \mathbf{5 0 \%}$ green light ($\mathbf{5 2 0} \mathbf{~ n m}$) flicker stimulation to awake rats.

articleTitle: AI-Enabled Fusion of Electrocardiograph and Demographics for Prediction of Acute Kidney Injury Onset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a commonly encountered medical problem that is associated with poor health outcomes in AKI survivors, including increased mortality and re-admission to the hospital. Despite their high-risk status, only a small fraction (${\lt}10 \%$) of patients receive specialized nephrologist follow-up after AKI event. To address the gap in care for AKI patients, this work proposes an artificial intelligence (AI) based fusion technique that combines patient’s single-lead electrocardiograph (ECG) and demographics to predict AKI recurrence 3-7 days before onset. The ECG data is analyzed with an on-chip reservoir-computer (RC) prototyped in 28nm CMOS process to create a compressed representation for predicting AKI onset from ECG. After fusion with demographics, the proposed technique is able to predict AKI recurrence 3-7 days before onset with 75.8% accuracy when evaluated on a retrospective patient dataset collected from Mayo Clinic Enterprise.

articleTitle: Leveraging RingConn Smart Ring for Monitoring Women’s Menstrual Health: A Pilot Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Women’s health is an important area of global public health research, encompassing numerous physical, psychological, and social dimensions. Among these, monitoring the menstrual cycle is a key aspect of health management. Currently, the menstrual cycle prediction mainly uses the method of recording historical dates, which relies on the self-report of the user and is subjective. However, with the advent of intelligent wearable technology, menstrual monitoring methods based on physiological indicators provide a more scientific approach. In this paper, we utilized temperature data monitored by the RingConn Smart Ring for trend analysis and predicted the next menstrual date based on the observed temperature trends. Among the recruited subjects, the prediction accuracy within ±3 days was 92.55%, verifying the method’s effectiveness and accuracy. This study lays the foundation for further exploration of menstrual prediction based on skin body temperature in the future.

articleTitle: A Novel AI-Inspired Method and System Implementation for Detecting and Classifying Pediatric Respiratory Sound Events
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Physicians utilize sound records for diagnosing respiratory diseases, but human error in judgment can lead to misdiagnosis and delay treatment. We propose an AI-inspired system separated into event detection and event classification. For event detection, we use voice activity detection to detect the presence of sound events. For event classification, we use the trained DenseNet model to classify various sound events associated with respiratory conditions. Ultimately, the process correlates sound events to different respiratory diseases based on the identified sound events. The F-score and Error Rate are 0.3296 and 1.36 for the overall evaluation metrics with the SPRSound dataset.

articleTitle: A 13.56-MHz 94%-PCE Active Rectifier with Timing-Mode Delay Compensation for Implantable Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: In this paper, a CMOS active rectifier with closed-loop timing-mode delay compensation has been proposed. It utilizes the switching of input pairs of comparators (CMPs) to introduce offset and relies on an edge-based feedback loop to define the timing for offset introduction. Compared with existing compensation methods, the proposed active rectifier can use much smaller power transistors as the additional power dissipation in offset introduction circuit has been eliminated in the CMPs. Hence it occupies a smaller footprint while achieving a competitive power conversion efficiency (PCE) and voltage conversion rate (VCR) to prior arts. The proposed active rectifier has been simulated in the Cadence Virtuoso environment using X-FAB’s $0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$ CMOS process. It occupies an area of $0.105 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. The simulation results show that the peak PCE is 94.0% with a $\mathbf{2 3 0}-\Omega$ load and the peak VCR is $\mathbf{9 8. 2 \%}$ with a $1-\mathrm{k} \Omega$ load when the active rectifier’s input is 3 V.

articleTitle: ST-BPTT: A Memory-efficient BPTT SNN Training Approach through Gradient-Contribution-Driven Time-Step Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer the advantage of mimicking the brain’s asynchronous and event-driven computation, enabling energy efficiency and robustness in information processing. Back-Propagation Through Time (BPTT) is a training approach for SNNs, which unfolds the computational graph across both time-step and space directions, and it is widely recognized for its high-accuracy training capabilities. However, the BPTT training approach encounters a significant challenge stemming from its high hardware memory consumption, necessitated by the storage of data from all time-steps. We introduce STBPTT, a memory-efficient BPTT-based SNN training approach that selects significant time-steps for gradient back-propagation computation. A gradient-contribution-driven strategy is proposed to help select proper time-steps. We have developed a PyTorch plugin compatible with SNN training frameworks to realize ST-BPTT. Evaluated across several SNN networks and diverse datasets, ST-BPTT can reduce memory consumption by up to $6.6 \times$ compared to the baseline, and by $1.9 \times$ compared to state-of-the-art BPTT-based training methods, with minimal impact on accuracy.

articleTitle: Compressed Frequency-Division Multiplexing Sampling Technique for High-Density NearInfrared Brain Functional Imaging Photoelectric Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Multi-channel and high-density fNIRS systems are crucial for providing detailed and comprehensive brain activity mapping, enhancing the understanding of neural processes. Currently, fNIRS primarily employs time-division multiplexing to sequentially collect data from each channel. However, as the number of channels increases, the time resolution significantly deteriorates. Therefore, maintaining high temporal resolution of fNIRS device represents the primary objective of this work. Therefore, this study introduces a compressed frequency-division multiplexing(FDM) sampling technique, considering the principle of light attenuation and the optoelectronic arrangement of the equipment, utilizing just four carrier frequencies to develop a multi-channel fNIRS system. This research verified the proposed solution through deployment on an FPGA platform and the measurement results ensures high temporal resolution of the device within highdensity fNIRS system photoelectric arrays.

articleTitle: Live Demonstration: Wireless Power Transfer Schemes for Brain Machine Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: This demonstration aims to provide visitors with hands-on experience to understand the impact of various Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) schemes on power transfer efficiency in implantable brain-computer interfaces (iBCIs) with mock-up LED-based receivers. The demonstration includes 2-coil, 3-coil, and 4-coil systems, as well as 2-coil systems with 1-layer or 2-layer resonators. Visitors will explore how different distances, alignments, orientations, and receiver sizes affect power transfer efficiency in various scenarios and solutions.

articleTitle: An Energy-efficient and Dual-mode AI Accelerator for Wearable Lung Sound Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
abstract: Lung diseases seriously impact human health. Using Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) to pre-diagnose lung diseases based on lung sounds is a growing trend. However, most existing DNN hardware accelerators perform direct finegrained multi-category classification for lung sounds, leading to low energy efficiency, as most lung sounds are normal, and only a coarse-grained classification for abnormal detection is sufficient for pre-screening. This paper proposes an energyefficient Artificial Intelligence (AI) accelerator based on a tightly Two-Stage Hybrid Neural Network (TS-HNN) model for wearable lung-sound monitoring applications. First, a TwoStage Data Buffering Scheme (TS-DBS) with a custom Local Memory Bank (LMB) is proposed to support the two-stage acceleration of the TS-HNN model. Second, by observing the channel correlation of two major convolution operators, a Reconfigurable Processing Element Array (RPEA) is designed for efficiently computing standard/pointwise convolution and depthwise convolution, enhancing the computation efficiency and energy efficiency. The FPGA experimental results show that the proposed AI accelerator can achieve an energy efficiency of 96.97 GOPs/W, and it only consumes $0.39 \mathrm{~mJ} /$ frame for normal lung sounds and $2.03 \mathrm{~mJ} /$ frame for abnormal lung sounds, which indicates energy efficiency improvement against the state-of-the-art design by $13.41 \times$ and $2.58 \times$, respectively.

articleTitle: Memory in Motion: Exploring Leaky Integration of Time Surfaces for Event-based Eye-tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Biomedical Circuits and Systems Conference (BioCAS)
